title: WMFA-AT: Adaptive Teacher with Weighted Multi-Layer Feature Alignment for Cross-Domain UAV Object Detection

problem.summary: UAV object detection relies heavily on labeled data and assumes consistent data distributions between training and deployment domains, leading to significant performance degradation under domain shifts.
statements: However, its heavy reliance on labeled data and the assumption of consistent data distributions between training and deployment domains limit its generalization ability, leading to significant performance degradation under domain shifts.
These constraints significantly weaken the generalization ability of the detectors when confronted with new domains, leading to a substantial performance drop in the presence of domain shift [13,14].
Substantial discrepancies in feature distributions across UAV images captured under diverse conditions limit detection accuracy.

background.summary: The paper tackles cross-domain UAV perception across cross-time, cross-camera, cross-view, and cross-weather scenarios using teacher-student semi-supervised learning baselines like Adaptive Teacher and Domain-Adaptive Faster R-CNN.

solution.summary: WMFA-AT adopts a teacher-student mutual learning paradigm, integrating domain adversarial learning with weighted multi-layer feature alignment and strong-weak data augmentation to effectively mitigate domain discrepancies.
solution.approach: The student model performs adversarial alignment using multiple domain discriminators applied to different feature layers, where layer-wise transferability weights adaptively align domain-specific features.
components: Teacher-student mutual learning paradigm with bidirectional knowledge exchange
Weighted multi-layer feature alignment (WMFA) where feature layers are adaptively weighted based on transferability
Multiple domain discriminators applied to different FPN feature levels for adversarial domain adaptation
Weak-strong data augmentation pipeline to enhance pseudo-label quality and suppress source domain bias

evidence.quote: WMFA-AT adopts a teacher-student mutual learning paradigm, integrating domain adversarial learning with weighted multi-layer feature alignment and strong-weak data augmentation to effectively mitigate domain discrepancies.

Specifically, the student model performs adversarial alignment using multiple domain discriminators applied to different feature layers, where layer-wise transferability is quantitatively estimated and used to adaptively weight the alignment process.

experiments.summary: Evaluated across four constructed cross-domain UAV benchmarks covering cross-time (day to night), cross-camera (UAVDT to VisDrone), cross-view (satellite to UAV), and cross-weather (sunny to rainy).

evidence.quote: Quantitative evaluations show that the proposed method consistently outperforms baseline and state-of-the-art methods, achieving substantial improvements in mAP50 across all tasks.

limitations.summary: Requires onboard compute efficiency optimizations and currently lacks multimodal sensor integration (e.g., thermal/infrared, LiDAR) for unconstrained dynamic edge environments.
items: Currently restricted to visible-band RGB sensors, lacking multimodal fusion with thermal infrared or LiDAR under extreme darkness.
Efficiency and stability for onboard edge deployment requires developing lightweight or sparse architectures.
Pseudo-label noise under severe distribution drift requires more reliable uncertainty-aware filtering mechanisms.

evidence.quote: First, we plan to extend the framework toward broader application scenarios, including multimodal sensing (e.g., infrared or LiDAR) and fully unsupervised or continual domain adaptation
Second, we aim to further improve the efficiency and stability of the adaptation process by developing lightweight or sparse architectures suitable for onboard deployment

applications.detail: Cross-domain aerial object detection under varying environmental conditions such as weather shifts and day/night transitions for autonomous UAV missions.
applications.quote: Overall, WMFA-AT demonstrates strong performance and generalization capabilities in domain-adaptive UAV object detection, establishing it as a promising solution for real-world UAV deployment in dynamic and unconstrained environments.
